        <h1>OpenPhish Feed Integration Guide</h1>
        <div class="meta">
            <span>📖 8 min read</span>
            <span><i class="fas fa-crosshairs"></i> Advanced</span>
            <span>📅 Updated: November 2025</span>
        </div>
    </header>

    <div class="content">
        <p>
            Phishing remains one of the most effective attack vectors, with over 90% of cyberattacks starting with a
            phishing email. OpenPhish provides a free, real-time feed of active phishing URLs that you can integrate
            into your security infrastructure to detect and block phishing attempts before they reach your users.
        </p>

        <h2>What is OpenPhish?</h2>
        <p>
            <a href="https://openphish.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">OpenPhish</a> is a fully automated platform that
            identifies phishing sites using proprietary Artificial Intelligence algorithms. The service provides:
        </p>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Real-time phishing URL feed</strong> - Updated continuously with newly discovered phishing
                sites</li>
            <li><strong>Free tier</strong> - Public feed with basic phishing URLs</li>
            <li><strong>Premium tier</strong> - Enhanced feed with additional metadata and faster updates</li>
            <li><strong>JSON and text formats</strong> - Easy integration into various security tools</li>
        </ul>

        <h2>Why Integrate OpenPhish?</h2>

        <h3>Proactive Defense</h3>
        <p>
            Block phishing URLs before they reach your users' inboxes. Email gateways, web proxies, and DNS filters
            can use OpenPhish data to prevent access to known phishing sites.
        </p>

        <h3>Incident Response</h3>
        <p>
            When investigating suspicious emails, quickly check if URLs are in the OpenPhish database. This helps
            triage potential phishing incidents faster.
        </p>

        <h3>Threat Hunting</h3>
        <p>
            Search your proxy logs, email logs, and DNS logs for historical matches against OpenPhish URLs to
            identify users who may have been targeted.
        </p>

        <h2>Understanding the OpenPhish Feed</h2>

        <h3>Feed Format</h3>
        <p>
            OpenPhish provides feeds in two formats:
        </p>

        <h4>1. Text Format (Free Tier)</h4>
        <pre><code>https://example-phishing-site.com/login

https://another-phishing-page.net/verify hxxps://fake-bank-login[.]com/account

        <p>
            Simple newline-separated list of phishing URLs. Easy to parse and integrate.
        </p>

        <h4>2. JSON Format (Premium Tier)</h4>
        <pre><code>{

“url”: “https://example-phishing-site.com/login”, “phish_detail_url”: “https://openphish.com/phish/…”, “submission_time”: “2025-11-26T12:34:56Z”, “verified”: “yes”, “target”: “PayPal”, “sector”: “Financial Services” }

        <p>
            Enhanced format with metadata including target brand, verification status, and submission time.
        </p>

        <h2>Integration Methods</h2>

        <h3>Method 1: Email Gateway Integration</h3>
        <p>
            Block phishing URLs at the email gateway level before they reach user inboxes.
        </p>

        <h4>Example: Proofpoint Integration</h4>
        <pre><code># Python script to fetch OpenPhish feed and update Proofpoint blocklist

import requests import json

Fetch OpenPhish feed

response = requests.get(‘https://openphish.com/feed.txt’) phishing_urls = response.text.strip().split(‘\n’)

Extract domains from URLs

domains = set() for url in phishing_urls: domain = url.split(‘/’)[2] # Extract domain from URL domains.add(domain)

Update Proofpoint blocklist via API

for domain in domains: # Add to Proofpoint blocklist # (Actual API call would go here) print(f“Blocking domain: {domain}”)

        <h3>Method 2: Web Proxy/Firewall Integration</h3>
        <p>
            Block access to phishing sites at the network perimeter.
        </p>

        <h4>Example: Palo Alto Firewall Integration</h4>
        <pre><code># Script to create custom URL category in Palo Alto

import requests import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

Fetch OpenPhish feed

Create XML for custom URL category

for url in phishing_urls[:1000]: # Limit to 1000 URLs ET.SubElement(list_elem, ‘member’).text = url

Push to Palo Alto via API

(Actual API call would go here)

        <h3>Method 3: SIEM Integration</h3>
        <p>
            Correlate OpenPhish data with security events to detect phishing attempts.
        </p>

        <h4>Example: Splunk Integration</h4>
        <pre><code># Splunk search to correlate web proxy logs with OpenPhish feed

index=proxy | lookup openphish_feed.csv url OUTPUT phishing_status | where phishing_status=“phishing” | stats count by src_ip, url, user | where count > 0 | table _time, src_ip, user, url | sort -_time

        <div class="highlight-box">
            <strong>Pro Tip:</strong> Schedule a daily job to fetch the OpenPhish feed and update your lookup table
            in Splunk.
        </div>

        <h3>Method 4: DNS Filtering</h3>
        <p>
            Block phishing domains at the DNS level using services like Pi-hole or Cisco Umbrella.
        </p>

        <h4>Example: Pi-hole Integration</h4>
        <pre><code>#!/bin/bash

Script to update Pi-hole blocklist with OpenPhish domains

Fetch OpenPhish feed

curl -s https://openphish.com/feed.txt > /tmp/openphish.txt

Extract domains and create Pi-hole format

cat /tmp/openphish.txt |
awk -F/ ‘{print $3}’ |
sort -u |
awk ‘{print “0.0.0.0 “ $1}’ > /etc/pihole/openphish-blocklist.txt

Reload Pi-hole

pihole restartdns

        <h2>Automation Script Example</h2>

        <p>
            Here's a complete Python script to fetch, parse, and integrate OpenPhish data:
        </p>

        <pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env python3

“”“ OpenPhish Feed Integration Script Fetches OpenPhish feed and integrates with security tools “”“

import requests import json import sqlite3 from datetime import datetime from urllib.parse import urlparse

class OpenPhishIntegration: def init(self, db_path=‘openphish.db’): self.feed_url = ‘https://openphish.com/feed.txt’ self.db_path = db_path self.init_database()

def init_database(self):
    """Initialize SQLite database for storing phishing URLs"""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute('''
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS phishing_urls (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            url TEXT UNIQUE,
            domain TEXT,
            first_seen TIMESTAMP,
            last_seen TIMESTAMP,
            status TEXT DEFAULT 'active'
        )
    ''')
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()

def fetch_feed(self):
    """Fetch latest OpenPhish feed"""
    try:
        response = requests.get(self.feed_url, timeout=30)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.text.strip().split('\n')
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        print(f"Error fetching feed: {e}")
        return []

def parse_url(self, url):
    """Extract domain from URL"""
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    return parsed.netloc

def update_database(self, urls):
    """Update database with new phishing URLs"""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    now = datetime.now()
    
    for url in urls:
        domain = self.parse_url(url)
        cursor.execute('''
            INSERT INTO phishing_urls (url, domain, first_seen, last_seen)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT(url) DO UPDATE SET last_seen = ?
        ''', (url, domain, now, now, now))
    
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    print(f"Updated database with {len(urls)} URLs")

def get_active_domains(self):
    """Get list of active phishing domains"""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute('''
        SELECT DISTINCT domain FROM phishing_urls
        WHERE status = 'active'
    ''')
    domains = [row[0] for row in cursor.fetchall()]
    conn.close()
    return domains

def check_url(self, url):
    """Check if URL is in phishing database"""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute('''
        SELECT url, first_seen FROM phishing_urls
        WHERE url = ? AND status = 'active'
    ''', (url,))
    result = cursor.fetchone()
    conn.close()
    return result is not None

def run(self):
    """Main execution"""
    print("Fetching OpenPhish feed...")
    urls = self.fetch_feed()
    
    if urls:
        print(f"Retrieved {len(urls)} phishing URLs")
        self.update_database(urls)
        
        # Export for other tools
        domains = self.get_active_domains()
        with open('phishing_domains.txt', 'w') as f:
            f.write('\n'.join(domains))
        print(f"Exported {len(domains)} unique domains")
    else:
        print("No URLs retrieved")

if name == ‘main’: integrator = OpenPhishIntegration() integrator.run()

        <h2>Best Practices</h2>

        <div class="success-box">
            <ul style="margin: 0;">
                <li><strong>Update frequently</strong> - Fetch the feed every 30-60 minutes for fresh data</li>
                <li><strong>Implement TTL</strong> - Remove URLs older than 7 days (phishing sites are often
                    short-lived)</li>
                <li><strong>Validate before blocking</strong> - Test URLs before adding to production blocklists
                </li>
                <li><strong>Monitor false positives</strong> - Track blocked URLs and investigate user complaints
                </li>
                <li><strong>Combine with other feeds</strong> - Use OpenPhish alongside PhishTank, URLhaus, etc.
                </li>
                <li><strong>Log everything</strong> - Keep records of blocked attempts for incident response</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <h2>Common Pitfalls</h2>

        <h3>1. Blocking Legitimate Sites</h3>
        <div class="warning-box">
            <strong>Problem:</strong> Occasionally, legitimate sites may be incorrectly flagged.
            <br><br>
            <strong>Solution:</strong> Implement a whitelist for known-good domains and provide users with a way to
            report false positives.
        </div>

        <h3>2. Stale Data</h3>
        <p>
            Phishing sites are often taken down quickly. Blocking a URL that no longer exists wastes resources.
        </p>
        <ul>
            <li>Implement automatic expiration for old URLs</li>
            <li>Periodically verify if URLs are still active</li>
            <li>Remove inactive URLs from blocklists</li>
        </ul>

        <h3>3. Performance Impact</h3>
        <p>
            Large blocklists can impact firewall/proxy performance.
        </p>
        <ul>
            <li>Limit blocklist size (e.g., 10,000 most recent URLs)</li>
            <li>Use domain-level blocking instead of full URLs when possible</li>
            <li>Optimize database queries for fast lookups</li>
        </ul>

        <h2>Measuring Effectiveness</h2>

        <p>
            Track these metrics to evaluate your OpenPhish integration:
        </p>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Blocked Attempts</strong> - How many phishing attempts were blocked?</li>
            <li><strong>User Reports</strong> - How many users reported blocked phishing emails?</li>
            <li><strong>False Positives</strong> - How many legitimate sites were incorrectly blocked?</li>
            <li><strong>Coverage</strong> - What percentage of phishing attempts are caught?</li>
            <li><strong>Response Time</strong> - How quickly are new phishing URLs blocked?</li>
        </ul>

        <h2>Advanced: Premium Feed Features</h2>

        <p>
            The OpenPhish premium feed provides additional metadata:
        </p>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Target Brand</strong> - Which company/service is being impersonated</li>
            <li><strong>Verification Status</strong> - Confidence level of phishing classification</li>
            <li><strong>Sector Information</strong> - Industry being targeted</li>
            <li><strong>Faster Updates</strong> - More frequent feed refreshes</li>
            <li><strong>Historical Data</strong> - Access to past phishing campaigns</li>
        </ul>

        <p>
            Premium feed enables more sophisticated detection rules:
        </p>

        <pre><code># Example: Alert on phishing targeting financial sector

if phishing_url.sector == “Financial Services”: if user.department == “Finance”: alert_priority = “HIGH” notify_security_team() else: alert_priority = “MEDIUM”

        <h2>Integration Checklist</h2>

        <ol>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Identify integration points
                (email gateway, proxy, firewall, SIEM)</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Set up automated feed
                fetching (cron job, scheduled task)</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Implement data storage
                (database, file, API)</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Configure blocklists in
                security tools</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Set up monitoring and
                alerting</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Create whitelist for false
                positive handling</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Implement TTL/expiration for
                old URLs</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Document integration for
                team reference</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Test with known phishing
                URLs</li>
            <li><i class="fas fa-check-circle" style="color: var(--accent-green);"></i> Monitor effectiveness and
                tune as needed</li>
        </ol>

        <h2>Conclusion</h2>
        <p>
            OpenPhish provides a valuable, free resource for combating phishing attacks. By integrating this feed
            into your email gateways, web proxies, firewalls, and SIEM systems, you can significantly reduce the
            risk of successful phishing attacks against your organization.
        </p>
        <p>
            Start with a simple integration—perhaps blocking at the email gateway level—and expand from there.
            Monitor effectiveness, tune for false positives, and combine with other threat intelligence feeds for
            comprehensive phishing protection.
        </p>

        <div class="highlight-box">
            <strong>Next Steps:</strong> Check out our <a href="/guides/threat-intelligence-soc.html">Threat
                Intelligence for SOC Analysts Guide</a> to learn how to integrate OpenPhish with other threat
            intelligence feeds.
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
